text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Secretary of State Madeleine Albright to visit in September. Internal closure lifted on Ramallah, Hebron.
- Moonies sponsor "Jewish Identity" meeting in Ariel next week.
- AT&T invests $15 million in Kardan venture fund.
- Finance Ministry director-general Shmuel Slavin: All ministries facing cuts in 1998.
- Industry and Trade Ministry: Plywood industry still not ready for imports.
GLOBES
- Histadrut trade union federation will on Sunday declare general work dispute.
- Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to spend holiday at private home in Caesarea, cancelling meals and services from Dan hotel.
- July CPI expected to rise 1.1 to 1.2 percent.
HAARETZ

- U.S. administration angry at Netanyahu. In Washington the claim is made he promised to cancel economic sanctions on the Palestinian Authority with the renewal of security coordination. Israel rejects the claim.
MAARIV
- Israel passes list of demands to Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat as a condition for easing of the closure.
- Three border policemen confess to brutality.

- Gallup poll: 57 percent of Jewish public satisifed with Netanyahu's handling of situation following attack, 39 percent not satisfied and 4 percent offer no response. If elections were held today, 42 percent would back Ehud Barak for prime minister, 38 percent Netanyahu, 20 percent don't know or respond but poll of 510 people taken this week has a 4.5 percent margin of error.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Syria tells Netanyahu: Let's resume negotiations immediately. Netanyahu says security arrangements preferable over normalisation with Arab states.
- New report by Holocaust survivors organisation in Israel shows Nazi war criminals get German government pensions higher than the compensation received by Jewish survivors.
